But the news at that time, as far as people in the local area was concerned, seems to be or the evidence seems to be that it came from one source only, and that's the famous radio Rama which was an HVO radio station or a station at least which was viewed by those on the other side as being a station that did not tell the truth, that was unreliable. And that radio station appears to have cried wolf once too often so now here when you have something happening at Uzdol which may - the Defence doesn't concede that it did - but may constitute a crime, no one believed them. Because they had lied too many times before. Now, Your Honours, that's the reason for calling the other witness that's going to be called, whose name you have. I won't say it now because we may -- I'm not sure what his position is going to be about protective measures and so on. But knowing his job, I foresee the possibility that like some other witnesses he might have some concerns about that. So -- but there is a soldier who went through the village on the Bosnian army side and he's chiefly being called because we want to ask him was he questioned and he's going to say, yes, he was. He's going to explain who it was who did it and he'll indicate what happened there. Now, you may or may not approve the findings that were made of that inquiry but they were made and you can see how they were made because those making the inquiry asked in good faith, were told what they were told and had no other way of investigating. And after that, those at the very senior level, including General Jasarevic, were prepared to sign off on a report and an opinion saying nothing happened. Now, it's -- in our -- our submission is that Halilovic was not obliged to involve himself in that in the least. But if you were against us on that you would find that what was required of him is exactly what happened, namely that an inquiry be made. Now, a witness -- just excuse me one moment, please, Your Honour. There is another witness who has been indicated to the Court and the Prosecutors, who is a UN person and his name would be necessarily subject to protective measures. He'll say something about how possible it was to get information on the HVO side at that time. And that's why he's being called. So we say in relation to that that the investigation had to be done at a local level. It was done at a local level. And all that could be done was. But in any event, it's never been shown that the accused man had any powers to initiate or conduct any investigation at that point. It has to be remembered what resources he had. He was in the inspection team. He had one military security officer. That person is Namik Dzankovic. That person was already tasked with looking after and looking into what occurred at Grabovica and he was on the terrain in Grabovica and residing in Jablanica. He seems to have played no part on the northern part of the front. If Halilovic was required to do anything, it's an interesting proposition to see what organs he was supposed to use, but let it be speculated that he should have used the local ones. Well, they were used. They did what they could. And it's a matter that we say was dealt with at a level lower than where Sefer Halilovic was. That's if they prove he was in command. Your Honours, I should just make a remark about effective control generally here. The issues of effective control elude local law and it is not necessary for the Prosecutor to prove that Sefer Halilovic was appointed the commander de jure just as it's not sufficient for them to prove that. But in this case, they've undertaken to prove that in their indictment. They said that he was both de jure and de facto commander. So in this case, although generally speaking a Prosecution can secure a conviction in the absence of a -- proving a de jure responsibility, in this case, the Prosecution need to prove de jure responsibility. They need to prove that. Because there is a distance between Sefer Halilovic and those troops, if they were troops, who committed the killings. I say that because at Uzdol there is clear evidence that there were present in the attack units who were not part of the army structure but were from the police. And no one has proved in Uzdol of course, who killed which person. And it's never been proved. So for those reasons -- the crime scene -- the crime scene matters in that regard but in terms of the de jure case that the Prosecution wants to mount, we urge you to pay very close attention to the order of the 30th of the 8th, the 30th of August. Now, that order -- just excuse me one moment. Sorry, I'm just going to procure a copy of it, Your Honour. I know we've -- we've all learnt it by heart to some degree in this case. While it's being found I think I can conduct myself by heart in any event. That order is relied on heavily by the Prosecutor because there really is no other basis for the de jure case. The map that was produced in court, which was signed off on at -- at Jablanica when Rasim Delic was present, that map speaks for itself. Sefer Halilovic signed it as Chief of Staff. Rasim Delic signed it as commander. And he said the words "odobrava," I have approved it. It's possible to construct an argument that a person who signs an order in that way may -- who signs an order as Delic did may not be the operative commander but it's an unpersuasive argument and we think we will be able to point out exactly why it fails. But in any event, it leaves that argument moot and the Prosecution desperately needs this order of the 30th and it's an order that speaks for itself. It creates an inspection team. And the inspection team has functions. Your Honours, I'm sorry, it's D146, Exhibit 146. It's on the screens now. It makes it clear that the team has to be formed - this is at point 1 - to coordinate the work and tasks in the zone of responsibility of the 4th and 6th Corps. So, if you like, the overarching purpose of this is set out there and it's coordination. Now then, in point 1, comes the famous reference to control of combat operations. The Defence says that it's just an incoherent reading of this order to suggest that that gives command of an operation to Halilovic. It's inconsistent with the foregoing sentence. It's inconsistent with the nature of an inspection team. It's inconsistent with prong number 3 there which gives actually a limited power to give orders. And I pose the question rhetorically, what's the need for a power to give orders, a limited power to give orders, in point 3 if Halilovic was being appointed a commander somewhere else in the order? Look to point 4. It says "the monitoring should begin on a certain date and be completed by," an unfilled-in date, "submit a report," that report orally, "on important questions during the inspection." Now, if combat activities were to last beyond the inspection date, what's the effect of this report? And what happens to this team that's created ones it reports, as it did, on the 20th of September? The Defence says that whilst there may be room for a couple of different interpretations of that order, you could not conclude to any standard of proof that this creates a command function in Sefer Halilovic. And that is their case, de jure. Really, it supports the thesis of the Defence more than it supports the Prosecution. We say that it says what it says it is. We say that it's quite clear what Sefer Halilovic's role was. He was the head of an inspection team. Why appoint him in point 2 as the head of an inspection team? You've seen orders here that have been tendered to make it quite clear how you appoint a commander. You appoint him as commander, or her as commander. You say who they are commanding, which units they are commanding. How long they command them for. And it's because of that search for some function for Halilovic outside of the obvious one which is head of the inspection team that the Prosecution came up with this idea of an operations group. Now, that really was a very admirable effort by the Prosecutors, and they should be intellectually praised for trying. It's worth a try. It's outside the pleadings, though, it's way outside them. And it's outside the evidence, too, because there was no operations group. There was none. No one at the time heard of it. There is no order creating it. There is no resubordination of units to it and that operations group didn't exist. And if the Prosecution are heard to argue that there was a quasi or partial operations group, then there is no evidence of that either, nor should they be granted the -- the right to argue that at a late time in the case when that does not appear in the indictment and is inconsistent with that indictment. So, Your Honours, at the end of that analysis of the Uzdol crime -- the Uzdol charge, and having looked at that order, I simply want to say that when it comes to the effective control argument the Prosecution want to run, they can't prove the -- excuse me a moment, I'm sorry, Your Honour. Sorry about that, Your Honour. They can't prove the de jure case and they can't prove any other form of appointment, any, if you like, de facto appointment. And at the other end of that equation is the question of whether the troops themselves were under the effective control, and because that's a matter that relies on many pieces of evidence I'm not going to rehearse it now as I indicated earlier, but you have to consider questions of whether or not those troops who were in Jablanica -- in Grabovica at the time of the killings were under anyone's control. Because what looks to have happened is that Ramiz Delalic came down to Jablanica with them and then left. It's possible that he went to the village, too. We don't know. He gave there account of being in Konjic and amusing himself there but that should be disregarded because the evidence was very strong that that's not what he did and it's not really consistent with his previous stories that he's told either. It looks as if he came down to Jablanica with them. Now, after that, he left and it would appear the evidence -- the weight of the evidence is that he wasn't present when the killing happened. We don't know but there is no evidence that he was there when the killing happened. And it really does appear perhaps -- I'm just reminded that there is actually some evidence that he was there earlier on in the afternoon. That has to be taken quite seriously. But in terms of presence during the crimes, the shootings and -- let it be clear there were some atrocities committed in Grabovica. But whether those troops were under anyone's control at that time is open because he came along, they were supposed to be resubordinated to Zulfikar Alispago, according to some evidence. Is it proved that Zulfikar Alispago had effective control over them? It's not. And all along that chain, it's not proved, and their very conduct suggests that they were not in control either. But in any event, I'll enter if I continue like that, I will enter into that area that we will keep to the end so I won't do it. So, Your Honours, that's what the Defence says. We have attempted to put here our case through the Prosecution and that's why it's appropriate to review the evidence rather than to introduce everything that's to come because there is not much to come. There really isn't. We intend to finish this with anyone a fortnight and if it wasn't for the fact that witnesses were ill or unable to dom this week it might be quicker. There remains -- I've got an administrative detail I'll come to later on. Finally it remains to this say: In terms of analysing our case it's too early for you to uphold any submission by me now. You have not -- I don't ask you to -- but it's important to understand where the case stands now, the Defence is asserting that the Prosecution have already failed. We are not now saying that we have a knockout punch or something new. We are saying that the Prosecution has now failed to meet its task. We are going to add some evidence to that, but that's what we say. And in light of that, we just make the final comment. It's a short case. Some people on the internet here -- internet here are saying it's the shortest case that's been run, but we have faith that running a short case is not in any way going to compromise the fair trial that we get. We have faith that the Tribunal will look at the evidence, not in search for the way the Prosecution puts its case but in search of the way the Defence puts its case, too. And, Your Honours, when you come to consider the evidence and when those who are assisting you in particular who perform an important job in helping you to do the work and to prepare things, when they come to consider the evidence, when you come to consider it, don't look to the Prosecution case simply to find the Prosecution evidence in it. That's where our evidence is. And we think when you look at the sensible, reliable witnesses, people like Namik Dzankovic, people like Vahid Karavelic, people who are sensible, people who didn't have an axe to grind, the victims from Grabovica, they were sensible witnesses, those people are the people on whose judgement you rely. Now, the Defence wants to point finally to the witnesses who we say you should disregard completely and we are not going to embark on why because that's something to do at the end of the case. But we say Ramiz Delalic is in a special category of his own. Not only should he be disregarded but you can trace back the damage to that he does to the Prosecution case through his evidence. He's in a special category because he's not just to be disregarded. He was a positive force for evil in the Prosecution case. He joined the Prosecution case back in the days when Mr. Mikhailov was the investigator. He procured witnesses. And it's a funny thing that the witnesses who came here from the 9th Brigade who were hostile to Mr. Halilovic was he, himself, Mr. Delalic, Witness D, and the two other individuals who were both -- who were all three associates of his during and after the war. The other people who were called, even those who were soldiers at Grabovica, did not say those things about Sefer Halilovic. And there was a real smell of collusion about those people because of the way their stories changed together. But the detail, that is for another time. We ask you not to set weight by the evidence of the witness Gusic, Salko Gusic. He was in the chain of command here. He played his part. He was very keen to distance himself. He had a position to protect. So although he attributes a great deal of command responsibility and influence to Sefer Halilovic, he has a reason to do that and you know about him two things: That it was his command that issued the order to the Prozor Independent Battalion to go into battle, and you know he told a false story to this Tribunal and he was caught red hot doing so concerning his knowledge of the operation. He said he didn't know the name of the operation and didn't see that map. But a reliable, sensible witness, Selmo Cikotic, gave evidence here and was not challenged by anyone. And he said that Gusic indeed did and was given tasks. And he's therefore a witness with a purpose to serve and whose evidence is proved to be wrong on significant points and should be disregarded. There was one other witness who had a pseudonym, who gave evidence of having seen Sefer Halilovic a day or so after the killings. Wasn't clear whether it was the 10th or the 11th, but it was evidence that he had seen him there. That person was Witness E. I know his name, I've just now forgotten his pseudonym. He was the witness who had that diary which Your Honours may recall and he for reasons of the way he gave his evidence and for the certain facts that were elicited about him during the evidence, we say he is also a witness who should be disregarded. There are other witnesses with whom we take issue on certain points. But generally speaking, the witnesses did the best they could. It's 11 years ago, and the Defence may identify problems with a witness, you don't have to take any notice of that, unless it's significant of something in the case. Your Honours, that's the end. Those are the remarks I wish to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just two clarifications. The first one is about the quotation you made. What is the name of the case? I believe that we missed it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There was two. There was the high command case, and there was Pohl, P-o-h-l. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I think the first, it may be Pohl.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Pohl, P-o-h-l. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The second question is about the famous document of 30th of August. Do you happen to know the completion time in the paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It wasn't there in the -- it's not on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Any information on that from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Not off-hand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe we need a break right now. We will have a 30-minute break and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if the parties have nothing to say at this stage, could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. Sorry, pardon me, Your Honour just raised a question before -- before the break concerning that the time for the inspection team to report, and if you just have regard to the final sentence it will say the control ends at the time of the report. I haven't got it on the screen anymore. Your Honour, in part 4 it says "submit a written report on return." So that then you can link that to the written report that was in fact issued and is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm afraid we have to wait a few minutes more. There is no protective measures for this witness, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, there isn't, Your Honour. I had in mind just to go into the private session just to ask where he lives and -- where he lives and where works. That's the only issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may inform us when the time comes. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection to that, those few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful for the Prosecutors' assistance there in that matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Mr. Morrissey, the witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Behlo. Would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: My name is Mehmed Behlo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we just briefly move into the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will move into the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Behlo. Would you mind just telling the Judges your age, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in September of 1993, were you a member of the 317th Brigade of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was your position in that brigade?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I was appointed as the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 317th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And how old were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I wasn't yet 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How many men were there in the 2nd Battalion which you commanded?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, over 400 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when did you take up your position as the commander of that battalion?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: In June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Before you became involved in the war, what military experience did you have?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: When performing my regular military service, I had received training in Zadar and after that course I received training in Ohrid. That was part of my regular military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. And before you took up the position as commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 317th Brigade, what combat experience did you have? Just keep this very brief, please, but what involvement in the fighting did you have before that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Before my duties or before the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. I really meant -- perhaps I'll ask the question again because it wasn't too good. How did you become involved in the war and what did you do before you became the commander of that battalion? Just as a very brief overview of that.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: When the war broke out, I was mobilised. Men from the Territorial Defence Staff which was in Gornji Vakuf at the time, issued me with a summons. I was then involved in organising Territorial Defence units and when the 317th Brigade was established, I was also engaged in carrying out similar tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I understand. Now, could you just indicate what -- which unit was the 317th Brigade subordinated to? In what line of command was that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: The 317th Brigade was part of the Zapar OG which had its command post in Bugojno, and all these formations were under the command of the 3rd Corps which was located in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, could you indicate what was the geographical zone of responsibility of the 317th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: The -- when the 317th Brigade was established, and after it had been established, it was active in the territory of Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And which part of that territory was your battalion concerned to defend?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: My battalion was on the left flank of the area of responsibility of the 317th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And which part of your brigade adjoined you on your right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I didn't have any physical contact with the brigade on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And on your left-hand side, who was your immediate -- which military formation was your immediate neighbour?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, my area of responsibility, was the area of responsibility of the -- or rather the area of responsibility of the 2nd Battalion, this was the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in which line of command was the Prozor Independent Battalion? Who did it report to?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: They were in the zone of responsibility of the 6th Corps, with its headquarters in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Where was the headquarters of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: The headquarters of my brigade was located in the centre of Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was your battalion headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: It was located in the Voljevac village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you have a -- do you know a village called Mackara?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. It was located within the zone of responsibility of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Were there any facilities at Mackara?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. There were a few small buildings and there was a house there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And did your battalion have any activities or any facilities at that particular village or location?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. There were some logistics facilities there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And where was the headquarters of the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: It was located in the village of Scipe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did it remain in the village of Scipe or was it moved to another location?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know a location called Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was located in September 1993 at Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: One of the command posts of the Prozor Independent Battalion was also located there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours I would like to show the witness a document that he produced and place this on the ELMO. Your Honours, this document I believe has been circulated by e-mail. It hasn't been uploaded as yet. We are going to have it scanned with the colour scanner because it's got a colour drawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe you ask some questions about where and how this map is drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be M5445.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Behlo, what is that document that's just been placed on the screen next to you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: This is a sketch of the area of my responsibility, of the area of responsibility of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. MR. MORRISSEY I wonder if that could be zoomed out, please, just slightly so that the edges can be seen. Very well, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when did you produce that particular drawing?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yesterday or the day before yesterday, I think. I think it was yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Thanks very much. Just do you have a pointer there in your hand? Yes, I see you do. Would you mind please pointing on that map, first of all, to the town of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: [Points]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I ask you in September of 1992, who was it who occupied and held that town -- in 1993, I'm sorry, did I say a different date?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: The HVO forces were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And approximately when did the HVO forces take that -- take possession of that town?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Roughly speaking it was in November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Would you just trace the approximate front line as you've drawn it on that map with the pointer, just so that the Judges can see and the Prosecution can see where the front line was?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Start on one edge and go to the other.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: This is the right-hand side of the area of responsibility. The line passed by the village of Dobrosin [phoen], which is where HVO forces were deployed. Then it continued through Crni Vrh, and extended to this part here that is called Menik. And here between two villages there was a link with the Prozor Independent Battalion. This is where it joined the Prozor Independent Battalion. On the other side, we have the area of responsibility of the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please now point to Voljevac, the headquarters of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: [Points]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please point to where the collection of villages called Uzdol is?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: [Points]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you say approximately what was the distance from Uzdol to Prozor town?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: It would be about ten kilometres or even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, near to Uzdol, were there some Bosniak villages called Here, Kute, and Scipe?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you just point out for the judges and the Prosecutor where those villages were? Or are?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: [Points]. This is the village of Here. Here we have the village of Scipe and a little further away we have the village of Kute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just to remind us, could you please point to where Dobro Polje is?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Dobro Polje was in the depth of the Prozor Independent Battalion's area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, just returning to your zone of responsibility, was there a hill there called Crni Vrh which you've marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you just please point to the whole hill running the pointer along it to show that -- the Court what is meant by Crni Vrh?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: [Points]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Near to Crni Vrh, is there an area called Makljen?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I don't know that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You probably don't know how I pronounce it but on the map you've marked there M-a-k-l-j-e-n.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes, there is a place called Makljen. It's a pass over the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And does a road run through that pass?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. As I have said, it's a mountain pass. It goes over the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could you indicate to the Tribunal and the Prosecutors what was the strategic importance from the HVO point of view of Prozor and of that road?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: There were HVO forces which were mainly concentrated in Prozor, and they used the Makljen pass, the road leading to Gornji Vakuf, to provide reinforcements and to deploy their forces in the village of Pidris primarily, and in Makljen, and from these positions, the artillery shelled Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And can you explain, what did you understand to be the situation of Uzdol and what did you know about any HVO units that were there, in particular?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I think that there were some reserve forces that were deployed there, forces for the defence line in the town of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I move to strike that or at least goat some clarification in he says I think. That's outside the jurisdiction of the area of his troops. Is he guessing or does he know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could ask some more questions, Mr. Morrissey, in this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours, but I don't want applications to strike like that to be made any more. However -- sorry, Your Honours, I just want to get the thing back up on the screen. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was your source of knowledge for what you knew about the troops in -- in Uzdol? Where did you get your information?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Well, I had certain information from the adjacent areas of responsibility, information that was relevant to my area of responsibility. And what I have in mind is in fact the deployment of HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you ever receive refugees or escapees coming across from HVO-occupied territory?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Thanks. MR. MORRISSEY Well, I offer that document for tender, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I indicate that we'll have that scanned and it will be in the E court format shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And the court deputy will tell us the number of that document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D446.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, that will be D445.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, in a few minutes, Mr. Behlo, I'm going to return that document to you to comment on the combat operations when we actually get to those but now I want to take you back a couple of weeks or two weeks or so before the combat operations. What was the first instruction you received concerning these -- the combat operations which ultimately happened on the 13th and 14th of -- and 15th of September?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Towards the end of August 1993, and at the beginning of September, we received preparatory order from the command of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And can you indicate which person you received -- can you recall which person you received those orders from?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. How was it that you received orders from the 6th Corps when your unit was as a matter of organic structure within the organisation of operations group Zapar and the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: There were individual orders that concerned combat action and they were received from the 6th Corps, and I had to inform my commander in the 317th Brigade of these orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I neglected to ask you but who was the commander of the 317th Brigade at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Enver Zejnilagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What did you understand to be his military experience?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: He was a high-ranking former JNA officer, and he had a lot of experience as a member of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, you referred to orders of the 6th -- coming from the 6th Corps command. What was the substance of those orders?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: The preparatory orders had to do with selecting a certain number of troops and deploying them at Dobro Polje, where they were to prepare to launch an offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And Dobro Polje being in part of the independent Prozor Battalion's area, was the Prozor Independent Battalion involved with this order?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And in practical terms, what efforts did you make to carry out these orders and what happened?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I ordered that some men from the 2nd Battalion unit be selected, men who were best prepared at that point in time to carry out the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what sort of things did those men do up at Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: They mostly carried out short training and worked on some military skills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in that time, was it required of you to liaise with Enver Buza, the commander of the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. I had to coordinate this task with Enver Buza.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Which person from the 6th Corps command did you have the most frequent contact with in that time, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, at some time, did you become aware of the impending visit of some senior generals from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: My commander, Zejnilagic, told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what did he tell you when you first heard about it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: That I should go with him to a meeting in Dobro Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you able to remember the date of that meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: It was sometime before the preparations. Actually, during the preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just giving your best estimation, about how long before the actual combat began do you recall this meeting taking place?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: About five days before, or slightly less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, who did you see -- or perhaps I should ask you the identities of the senior people who came from Sarajevo. Who did you understand was coming?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: General Halilovic, Karic, and the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, can you remember which ones of those individuals you actually met yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: There was this preparatory meeting. I was with my commander, and that was the first time I saw General Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And who else was there, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I know that commander Cikotic was there, and the commander of the 6th Corps, Gusic. I cannot remember the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what happened at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Nothing special. The meeting didn't last very long, and logistical needs were mostly discussed for units that were already in Dobro Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And which units are you talking about which were in Dobro Polje? Are they the ones you referred to earlier on or different units?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the ones that were there as well as others of the that was when I heard that other units were supposed to arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you meet an individual named Bilajac, Rifat Bilajac?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And where did you meet Bilajac? And in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I first had contact with him in the village of Voljevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And was that before or after this meeting at Dobro Polje, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: It was after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what happened in your meeting with Mr. Bilajac? Who was there and what did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: At the invitation of my commander, Mr. Zejnilagic, I came for a brief consultation which was also attended by General Bilajac, actually Rifat Bilajac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What contribution did Mr. -- Did General Bilajac make to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: He just wanted to hear about the preparations that I had carried out, what plan I was proposing. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when you told him about what plan you were proposing, what did he say and what did he do?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: He continued the conversation with my commander, Zejnilagic, and explained some details to me. Actually, he gave me some instructions about how to implement the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what an operations group is?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, at the time of the planning of this -- of these combat operations, did you ever hear it suggested that Sefer Halilovic had come down to lead an operations group in that area?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Very leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's a very leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- well, if Your Honour thinks it is, I'll deal with it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was the topic of an operations group raised by any person in the context of those combat operations in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: At the time, there was no operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Given what you know of an operations group, was Sefer Halilovic of an appropriate level of seniority to command an operations group?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if there is an operation there must be somebody who will lead that operation. You may just ask a blank question seeing that -- who was leader of that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It depends on the answer of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I can certainly ask him that question but the Prosecution have raised an issue here which is why -- I won't make a comment -- but they wish to say there was an operations group. So I'm going to ask him whether there was an operations group, as a person who was actually there. And Your Honour, your question is the right one. I will ask that, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe the witness has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. At the time when these combat operations were being planned, did you know who was in command of the operation, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: It was an operation that didn't have a sufficient number of units, and its task wasn't so big for an operative group, operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who did you report to through the course of your involvement in these combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I was implementing the direct orders much my commander, Zejnilagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you ever resubordinated to an operations group?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Later, in the course of the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In the course of these combat operations in September of 1993, though, was your battalion ever resubordinated to an operations ...

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: No. It wasn't part of any operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was the Prozor Independent Battalion resubordinated to an operations group at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in what -- well, to whom was the Prozor Independent Battalion reporting in the course of those combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Of course, under the command of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in the time that you -- in the time of preparation for these combat activities, what did you see with your own eyes Sefer Halilovic doing? Perhaps I could ask you this first of all: How many times did you see Sefer?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Twice all together in the course of the operation. Once in Dobro Polje and the second time in a place called Mackara.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I want to move now to the combat operations themselves. Can you recall the precise date at which you went into action for the first time on Crni Vrh?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: That was the night of the 12th and the morning of the 13th of September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And pursuant to what plan did you go into action on Crni Vrh?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: On the basis of a plan drafted by myself and commander Zejnilagic

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now,?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness just have that exhibit that was on the ELMO, please, returned? And I just ask that the Court staff assist with that. It's Exhibit 445. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnilagic [sic], I'm just going to ask you to indicate now what the plan involved for your troops, and then what it involved for the Independent Prozor Battalion to your left. Okay. Now, on that map, it's apparent that there are three green arrows. Can you explain what those three green arrows represent?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: These are the axes of attack which should have been carried out from the staging positions in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could you just explain what the purpose of those attacks was? Why did you -- why did -- why did you want your soldiers to go there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: During earlier estimates and earlier actions, we always tried to capture the Crni Vrh area and the Makljen mountain pass and the Makljen Blace lines, to take -- to capture the Makljen-Blace village line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And if you succeeded in capturing that area, what was the consequences for further attacks on Prozor?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: It meant a lot for the entire front in Gornji Vakuf, because it would be cutting off the supply lines and the forces out in the Gornji Vakuf area would be cut off completely. I think those were HVO forces. And as the action continued, a large area of the Prozor territory would be placed under control from this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was the Prozor Independent Battalion supposed to do on the morning of the 13th when you went into action?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: According to the plan, the Prozor Independent Battalion had to resubordinate a part of its forces to my commander, Zejnilagic, in order to carry out the task. While the rest of the units were supposed to tie up the forces at their own level of defence. And thereby assist the attack along the main axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can you just explain what the benefit was of the attack on Uzdol by the remaining forces of the Prozor Independent Battalion, as far as the operation?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: It wouldn't really have any effect on the implementation of the operation, because the Uzdol position was a passive one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And -- very well. So did Buza's forces, the Prozor Independent Battalion, go into attack on Uzdol on that day, the 13th, or not?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What happened to your troops when they attacked Crni Vrh on that day, the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: We had a plan whereby the forces that came as reinforcements, these were forces of the Sutjeska Battalion and the forces from the Neretvica Battalion, they were supposed to attack first, at the highest peak of Crni Vrh mountain which is called Sljeme. And as the situation developed, my unit reinforced by the Prozor forces was supposed to capture the Zgon area and especially the positions in the area of the village of Blace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what went wrong?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: The first axis that actually the attack along the first axis after the initial success achieved, was cut off abruptly and it failed because one of the commanders of the Neretvica Battalion was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was the name of that commander who was killed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: That was Commander Padalovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And perhaps to come to the conclusion of that day, at the end of the day, did you hold any extra territory or were you back where you started?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: No. We were stopped by the HVO forces and were forced to withdraw to our starting positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: At the end of the day, did the soldiers have any attitude or did any of you in fact have any attitude to the Independent Prozor battalion's failure to go into combat that day?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: The fighters were disappointed when they heard that the commander was killed, Commander Padalovic, and then there were some rumours also relating to the Prozor Independent Battalion and their activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what were those rumours?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Someone said that the soldiers were playing soccer in Dobro Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let's move to the 14th, the following day. To your information, did the Prozor Independent Battalion then go into battle the following day?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: After the failure of the first day, a brief analysis was carried out, and some actions were expected on the left flank, on the left side of the Prozor Battalion, which would then encourage my soldiers and the soldiers from the reinforcement to continue attacks along our axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what did the Prozor Independent Battalion do? Did they go into that attack? And how did they go?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: There were some actions but we didn't know what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And on the 14th -- well, perhaps I won't ask you about the 14th. Did you hear the results of whether the Prozor Independent Battalion succeeded in their attacks? I understand you say not in specifics. But did you hear generally speaking whether they succeeded or failed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Their success or, rather, our success did not depend on their success.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: We, the next day, again did not succeed in our task. Later, we heard briefly that the soldiers from the Prozor Independent Battalion went into a minefield and that's how they got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Now I'd like to show you an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 150? It's the Zejnilagic order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, this document is about to be brought up on the computer screen here and I just ask you to have a look at it when it comes up. All right. Do you have that document? Do you have on your screen there a document headed "order to attack" and dated 15th of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, just to be -- just to complete some formalities first of all, do you recognise this order?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. I participated in the drafting of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'll ask you how that was done in just a moment. Could I just ask you to have a look, please, at point number 4 on the order. Is that -- does that appear on your screen? Your Honours, for the English it will have to be turned over to the following page. Mr. Behlo, is point 4 visible to you there or not?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see there that there is a reference to combat activities on the 16th of September?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I ask you to please have a look at point number 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think in the English, Your Honours, it will have to be turned over to the next page. And Bosnian, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see there the date of the 15th of September and the section that says "in the course of 15 September 1993 all units shall send IP reconnaissance patrols and OG reconnaissance groups to reconnoiter the axis of attack against the enemy." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Okay, well, now, perhaps, just in your own words can you explain what happened? Why was that order drafted and what part did you play in drafting it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Well, since we failed to carry out our order during the first two days of the operation, we failed to take control of the Crni Vrh feature, we had to change and amend our initial plan. And this was done by virtue of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Would you just --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the start of that order once again, just go back to the start of that order. So page 1 of both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you see in the preamble to that order, the preamble refers to two orders on which you based or yourself and Zejnilagic based this order? Do you see those references?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Just before -- and those orders are identified, one of them, is that correct, as an order of the NGS Chief of Staff, and the other one is identified as a command of the commander of the 6th Corps with an order number 01/1500-27, dated 11 September 1993? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm going to take you to some orders in just a moment. I just want to ask you now what happened in relation to this particular order? How did the combat pan out and what occurred? So it says in the order that you have to conduct intelligence on the 15th and go into battle on the 16th. Can you just explain to the Judges and the Prosecutor what happened?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Well, after the failure on the 13th and 14th, after the failure of the action, we regrouped and consolidated the units in the areas which were -- where they initially had their positions. We carried out additional reconnaissance on new axes of attack. This reconnaissance was carried out on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Could I just ask that the witness be shown another map and I'll ask him some questions about it. I think this will be Exhibit -- MFI 446.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Could you just, now, pointing on that map indicate what happened on the morning of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Having carried out the preparations on the 15th, we set off in the evening with the units and went to our initial positions from which we were to launch an attack, and according to the new amended order, we had selected new axis of attack, which was on the village of Glibe axis and further on, along the same axis, there was the village of Blace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could you just explain a bit about that map? First of all, who produced it and when?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I made this sketch yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you just indicate is that a more close-up view of that combat area compared to the previous map?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. It's not clear in the first map, and the lie of the ground is clearer in this sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Could you just, using the pointer, point to whereabouts Prozor is? I understand it's not indicated on the map but just point approximately where one could find Prozor?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Prozor is somewhere around here, behind this hill, and in the direction of the village of Blace or rather behind the village of Blace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, just -- I'll just lead on something here. If the Prosecutor wants to object they can. Was the plan to go up behind the village of Blace on this occasion and attempt to conquer it from a different direction?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So just tell the Judges what happened.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Our forces remained on the Zgon-Blace axis but they were on a secondary axis and the focus of the attack was to be on the Rac-Glibe axis. I personally led a unit which was on this axis but when we entered the initial area from which the attack was to be launched, we ran into an HVO reconnaissance group which had approached us from behind. There was a brief clash, and when we decided to follow them we entered a mine field located right in front of the village of Glibe in this densely forested area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I offer that -- sorry, perhaps I should just ask finally, was there any more offensive combat operations after that time in that sector?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: I informed my commander, commander Zejnilagic, that we weren't in a position to continue carrying out the task in spite of having made several attempts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. After that time, did you see Sefer Halilovic in that area again? And I'm talking now about a period of about six weeks.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see Bilajac, Suljevic, Karic again in that time n that six weeks?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit number 124? I offer that map for tender, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D446.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What's coming up on the screen now is an order signed by Sefer Halilovic dated the 15th of September 1993. Okay. Do you have that order there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes. I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you recognise that order?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: It's an order that concerns my commander, Enver Zejnilagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And we noticed earlier on that there was reference in the preamble of the Zejnilagic order of the 15th of September to an order of the Chief of Staff. What do you say about this order? Is this the same or different?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: That's the order in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And do you know what lay behind the drafting of that order? Perhaps I should ask you: Were you present when that order was drafted?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: No. I wasn't present when this order was drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you know what power Sefer Halilovic had to issue an order like that? Or not an order like that, perhaps I'll get more specific. Do you know what power Sefer Halilovic had to issue that order?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There should be a foundation laid as to the basis for this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have the previous document which says very clear, so I believe that is the foundation for this question. You may proceed, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a different question. He's now asking what basis did he have, what powers did he have, if that's the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether that's a different question or the same question. I will let Mr. Morrissey continue for a while to see whether it's a leading question or not. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right, then. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you know -- I just want to ask the question the same way. Did you know what power Sefer Halilovic had to issue that order?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: No. I didn't know what power the Chief of Staff, General Halilovic, had, but I knew what sort of power my commander had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And do you know what was the need or the reasons behind the issuing of that order of the 15th by Sefer Halilovic that you have on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: Since we had failed, since our operation was a failure, it was essential to do something in order to carry out the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you yourself see Sefer Halilovic on that occasion signing that order?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just wonder, there is another document, Your Honour. It might take us a little bit longer so perhaps this is an appropriate moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that we'll break now. Well, Witness, since you are still under the oath, so I have to remind you that please do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. We'll continue your testimony tomorrow morning. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do understand you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The hearing for today is adjourned. We'll resume tomorrow morning.
